answer: Agents sell telescope-control code for tracking a comet near the zenith in an onyx sky. Buyers require a machine-checkable proof that each program obeys fixed mount-angle limits. An audited verifier decides acceptance, and account votes cannot override a failed check. A thousand aliases therefore cannot manufacture approval for code lacking a valid proof. This protects the specified property only: a flawed specification or verifier can still admit bad code, and submission spam needs a separate defense.
